Relevance against exclusion violation

Source: R/plot.R
plot.shadow_screen.Rd

Scatter of the screen: exclusion violation on the horizontal axis, relevance on the vertical, both incremental McFadden \(R^2\) on the same scale, with the equality line dashed. Above the line a candidate predicts the outcome better than it predicts selection. The line is not the border between usable and unusable: under strong selection on the outcome a validly excluded candidate shows exclusion signal through the outcome and sits close to it (see shadow_screen()). Points are labelled directly rather than through a legend; labels are placed so that they do not overlap each other or the points.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'shadow_screen'
plot(
  x,
  scale = c("log", "linear"),
  label = NULL,
  col = scan_colors[["sharp"]],
  text_col = "grey20",
  xlab = expression("Exclusion violation, incremental McFadden " * R^2),
  ylab = expression("Relevance, incremental McFadden " * R^2),
  main = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A "shadow_screen" object.

scale

"log" (default) or "linear" axes.

label

Candidates to label. Default: all if there are at most fifteen, else the most relevant one and the one with the highest ratio.

col

Point colour.

text_col

Colour for text and reference lines.

xlab, ylab, main

Axis labels and title.

...

Passed to graphics::plot.default().

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

Both measures typically span several orders of magnitude, so the default is logarithmic axes, on which the equality line is still the diagonal of the square plotting region. Values of zero are drawn at the lower axis limit. Distance from the line reads as a factor; distance along it as size. Read the relevance itself too: a candidate far above the line with negligible relevance is no shadow variable (see relevance_chisq_df). Rejected candidates are drawn grey and labelled "rejected", so that a weak candidate above the line is not mistaken for a pass. Hollow points mark candidates whose exclusion violation is at noise level (ratio_readable is FALSE): no violation is measured, their horizontal position is not estimated, and their label gives no ratio.

Examples

d <- simulate_shadow(5000, tilt = -1, seed = 1)
plot(shadow_screen(d, "y", "observed", c("x1", "x2"),
                   c("z_shadow", "z_policy", "z_score")))
